chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hannan ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'The two edges of the Bridge (as-Sirat) on the Day of Resurrection are Kinship (Ar-Rahim) and Trust/Entrustment (Al-Amanah). So when the one who maintains kinship and fulfills the trust passes by, he will pass through to Paradise. And when the betrayer of the trust and the cutter of kinship passes by, no deed will benefit him alongside these two, and the Bridge will fling him into the Fire.'

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge over Hellfire on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What are the two edges of the Sirat bridge on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (AS) from the companion Abu Dharr, highlights the dual pillars of social and spiritual integrity: maintaining kinship (Silat al-Rahim) and fulfilling trusts (Al-Amanah). In Shia scholarship, these are often viewed as the external manifestations of internal faith, where severing ties or betraying trust nullifies the efficacy of other good deeds, causing the believer to tip into Hellfire despite their efforts.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Hannan Bin Sadeyr, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Abu Zarr<sup style="font-weight: normal">ra</sup> said: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">ra</sup> heard Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> saying: ‘On the two edges of the Bridge on the Day of Judgement would be the kinship and the entrustment. So when the maintainer of the relationships and the fulfiller of the entrustments passes by, would pass throught to the Paradise, and when the betrayer of the entrustment, the cutter of the relationships passes by, the deeds would not benefit him along with these two, and the Bridge would fling him into the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma’il ibn Bazi’ from Hanan ibn Sadir from his father from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu Dhar (may Allah be pleased with him) has said, ‘I heard the Messenger of Allah saying, “On the Day of Judgment the bridge will stand on two pillars: the kindred relations and safe keeping of trust. Those who maintain good relations with relatives and return the trust will pass the bridge safely to paradise but when the abuser of trust and neglector of good relations with relatives will try to pass the bridge no other deeds will benefit him and he will be thrown off the bridge into the fire.’”
